name: LatinCy la_core_web_sm/md/lg 3.9.8
what: spaCy pipelines for Latin by Patrick J. Burns: enclitic splitter, tagger, morphologizer, edit-tree lemmatizer + lookup lemmatizer, parser, NER.
coverage: wheels: sm 19.19 MB, md 72.88 MB (50k floret vectors), lg 296.94 MB (200k vectors); trained on UD Perseus/PROIEL/ITTB/LLCT/UDante/CIRCSE + LASLA v1.0.1 + LatinCy NER
licence_quote: license: mit | | **License** | `MIT` |
accuracy_claim: README '### Accuracy' (v3.9 measurement, not re-measured for 3.9.8): LEMMA_ACC sm 94.98 / md 95.19 / lg 95.26; POS_ACC 96.85 / 97.25 / 97.26; MORPH_ACC 89.20 / 90.20 / 90.37. meta.json inside the sm 3.9.8 wheel: lemma_acc 0.9378, pos_acc 0.9552. arXiv 2305.04365 abstract: lemmatization 94.66%.
notes: Verdict reason: weights MIT, pip-installable from the HF wheel, runs on CPU. Two caveats to decide: (1) hard runtime dependency la-latincy-lookups (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 dataset) feeds `lookup_lemmatizer`; for a clean licence run with that component disabled, or ask the author; (2) training data includes NC treebanks (ITTB, PROIEL, Perseus) and LASLA (NC). Tokenizer behaviour (read from functions.py in the sm wheel, sha256 2175392…): LatinTokenizer strips macrons and ligatures and inherits spaCy lang/la rules; `normer` sets token.norm_ = lower().replace('v','u').replace('j','i') without changing the text; `uv_normalizer` (latincy-preprocess, MIT) restores a u/v distinction by rules; `enclitic_splitter` splits ONLY -que/-qve (not -ne, not -ue/-ve) with a 130-word exception list (atque, neque, quisque, uterque …). Lemma spelling convention (u vs v) must be checked on the 300-token test because LASLA training data is u-only ('nouus') while UD treebanks vary. PyPI has no la-core-web-* packages (404); install is `pip install <HF wheel URL>`.

name: LatinCy la_core_web_trf 3.9.8
what: Transformer variant of LatinCy (bert-base-multilingual-uncased per the training repo README); same components plus trf_vectors.
coverage: wheel 1,688.56 MB; same training data as sm/md/lg
licence_quote: license: mit | | **License** | `MIT` |
accuracy_claim: README '### Accuracy': LEMMA_ACC 95.48, POS_ACC 98.32, MORPH_ACC 95.78, DEP_LAS 84.38; model-index Lemma Accuracy 0.9463.
notes: Best LatinCy numbers but 1.7 GB and transformer inference; above this survey's 50 MB download cap, so untested here. Same NC caveats as sm/md/lg.

name: la-latincy-lookups 1.0.0 (LatinCy lookup table)
what: Latin lemma_lookup table registered through spaCy entry points; required by all la_core_web_* 3.9.8 wheels.
coverage: lemma_lookup: 909,669 entries from Kaikki Wiktionary + UD treebanks (README table)
licence_quote: [CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/). This package is a dataset, so it carries a content license rather than a software license. The lookup data is derived from Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 3.0) and Universal Dependencies treebanks (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0); the non-commercial terms of UD PROIEL and ITTB require the NC clause.
notes: NC. Needed to install LatinCy (Requires-Dist in the wheel METADATA) but the `lookup_lemmatizer` component can be disabled at load time; the table must not be copied into Melos data. LICENSE file head: 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International | Copyright (c) 2026 Patrick…'.

name: latincy-preprocess 0.5.1
what: U/V normalisation (u-only text to u/v), long-s OCR fix, macron stripping; spaCy components used by LatinCy (uv_normalizer).
coverage: rule-based; Rust-accelerated optional
licence_quote: MIT License  Copyright (c) 2026 Patrick J. Burns
notes: Useful on its own for form normalisation in the linter.

name: CLTK Latin backoff lemmatiser (cltk<=1.x + lat_models_cltk)
what: NLTK-style backoff chain (dictionary, unigram, regexp, Roman numerals, principal parts) with pickled models; CLTK 1.x `cltk.lemmatize.lat.LatinBackoffLemmatizer`.
coverage: lemmata/backoff pickles; lemmata/collatinus (lemmes.la, modeles.la …) converted from Collatinus; training sentences from AGLDT v2.1
licence_quote: The sentences models (latin_lemmatized_sentences.py and latin_pos_lemmatized_sents.pickle) are based on treebank data from [The Ancient Greek and Latin Dependency Treebank v2.1](https://perseusdl.github.io/treebank_data/) available under [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/us/) licence.
accuracy_claim: None stated. The class docstring (cltk v1.4.0 lat.py) calls it 'BETA Version of the Backoff Lemmatizer'.
notes: Code MIT (lat_models_cltk LICENSE: 'The MIT License (MIT) Copyright (c) 2014 Classical Language Toolkit'; cltk LICENSE MIT). Collatinus-derived data inherits GPLv3 (lemmata/collatinus/README.md). CLTK master (2.5.1, commit 33e1653) no longer has a `lemmatize` package: its Latin pipeline is Stanza-based with optional LLM backends, and evaluation/comparison_report_lati1261.md is an 8-token backend-agreement check, not an accuracy figure. The v1.4.0 source (sha256 34131a0f…) was fetched for reference.

name: Collatinus 12 (biblissima/collatinus)
what: Qt desktop lemmatiser + morphological analyser + scansion tool that inflects from a lemma lexicon instead of form lists; server mode with a Client_C11 command-line client; online Collatinus-web.
coverage: lemmes.la 24,072 lemma lines + lem_ext.la 57,909 extension lines (= 81,981); modeles.la paradigms; LASLA-derived frequencies and a probabilistic tagger (doc-usr/licence.md credits LASLA)
licence_quote: Collatinus is developed and maintained by Yves Ouvrard and Philippe Verkerk. It is made available under the [GNU GPL v3](http://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl.html) licence.
notes: Data licence: lemmes.la header says 'COLLATINUS and PRAELECTOR are free software; you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by the Free Software Foundation; either version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.' GPL copyleft applies to the lexicon file if redistributed, so use it as a separate tool (server + Client_C11, doc-usr/server.md: `./Client_C11 -lfr arma`) rather than bundling lemmes.la into Melos data; its lemma list is a candidate headword list only with GPL compliance. No Python API in the repo; PyCollatinus (PonteIneptique/collatinus-python, GPL-3 LICENSE file, PyPI metadata says 'GNU GPL v2', last release 0.1.6) is a stale port. Collatinus-web offers Gaffiot, Lewis & Short, Georges, Jeanneau, du Cange lookups online.

name: Whitaker's WORDS (mk270/whitakers-words)
what: Ada program: Latin-English dictionary with inflectional morphology; for a form it returns stem + inflection analysis (e.g. 'am.o V 1 1 PRES ACTIVE IND 1 S') and glosses.
coverage: DICTLINE.GEN 39,335 entry lines (site: 'over 39000 entries'); INFLECTS.LAT 3,228 lines of inflection rules; 6.1 MB dictionary
licence_quote: Permission is hereby freely given for any and all use of program and data. You can sell it as your own, but at least tell me. … All parts of the WORDS system, source code and data files, are made freely available to anyone who wishes to use them, for whatever purpose.
notes: No LICENSE file (404); the statement above is Whitaker's own, quoted in the README 'Licensing' section. Needs gnat/gprbuild to build. DICTLINE format: fixed-width columns — four stems (19 chars each), part of speech, declension/conjugation + variant, kind, then age/area/geography/frequency/source codes, then the English meaning string. Python port blagae/whitakers_words is MIT ('The MIT License (MIT) Original work Copyright (c) 2014-2017 Archimedes Digital'); not on PyPI (404). Gives glosses but terse; good as a fallback analyser and for the form inventory.

name: Morpheus Latin stem library (PerseusDL/morpheus stemlib/Latin)
what: The Latin half of Perseus Morpheus: stem sources, end tables and rule files compiled by the stemlib makefile; run with `MORPHLIB=stemlib bin/cruncher < wordlist`.
coverage: stemsrc/ls.nom 136,212 lines (nominal stems from Lewis & Short), vbs.latin 17,161 lines, plus irregulars, proper names (smithbio/smithgeo); 169 Latin paths
licence_quote: Unless otherwise indicated, all contents of this repository are licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 United States License. You must offer Perseus any modifications you make.
notes: Same licence and build as the Greek Morpheus Melos already runs; the local image (deploy/morpheus-local) builds the Greek stemlib only, so a Latin build is a new container, not a config change. Output is analyses with L&S lemma keys, which fits the Greek lemma-index design (parser lemmas → dictionary headwords).

name: LatMor (Springmann, Schmid, Najock)
what: Finite-state Latin morphology (SFST) returning lemma with vowel length and morphosyntactic tags; compiled transducers for download.
coverage: not stated on the page
licence_quote: LatMor is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. Before using LatMor for commercial purposes, you must purchase a license.
notes: NC plus paid commercial licence. Not downloaded.

name: LEMLAT 3.0 (CIRCSE/LEMLAT3)
what: Morphological analyser and lemmatiser with an embedded MySQL lexical database and command-line client (Linux/macOS/Windows builds in the repo).
coverage: not stated in README; repo 492 files incl. lemlat_db.sql
licence_quote: LEMLAT 3.0 is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License.
accuracy_claim: None stated. README: 'LEMLAT analyzes *types*, not *tokens*; it doesn't therefore disambiguate words in context.'
notes: Zenodo record 1492134 confirms 'Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial Share Alike 4.0 International'. NC bars production use; it is the lexical backbone of LiLa (LiLa lemmas carry LemLat relations), so LiLa (CC BY-SA) is the usable route to the same lemma inventory.

name: LatinPipe (ÚFAL, EvaLatin 2024 winner)
what: PhilBerta-based joint tagger/lemmatiser/parser; code MPL-2.0; released model latinpipe-evalatin24-240520 on LINDAT; also served by the LINDAT UDPipe REST service.
coverage: trained by sampling seven Latin corpora (UD 2.13 treebanks, harmonised PROIEL, Sabellicus, Archimedes Latinus); model 614.14 MB
licence_quote: This item is Publicly Available and licensed under: Creative Commons - Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
accuracy_claim: README: 'the winning submission to the EvaLatin 2024 Dependency Parsing shared task'; no lemma accuracy figure in the README.
notes: Code LICENSE: 'Mozilla Public License Version 2.0' (fetched). The model is NC, so it can serve as a comparison system in the 300-token test (via the LINDAT REST API or a local run) but not as the production parser. HF search found only third-party copies (bowphs/latinpipe-evalatin, card 404).

name: Stanza Latin models (stanfordnlp/stanza-la)
what: Stanza tokenizer/MWT/POS/lemma/depparse models per UD Latin treebank (ittb, llct, perseus, proiel, udante, circse), default package = ITTB.
coverage: models/default.zip 224.2 MB; whole repo 1,115.7 MB; lemma models ~2 MB each, pos ~20 MB, pretrain conll17.pt 107 MB
licence_quote: license: apache-2.0
accuracy_claim: Stanza performance page (Lemmas column): ITTB 99.09, LLCT 98.09, PROIEL 96.86, Perseus 83.57, UDante 86.95.
notes: Model card says Apache-2.0 (code LICENSE: 'Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0') but the models are trained on CC BY-NC-SA treebanks (ITTB, Perseus, PROIEL, UDante); only the LLCT and CIRCSE models rest on CC BY-SA data. The Perseus (classical) lemma score of 83.57 is the relevant one for poetry and is low. Candidate for the contextual rescoring role the Greek index gives OdyCy, if the licence reading is accepted.

name: UDPipe 2 Latin models (ÚFAL, UD 2.17)
what: UDPipe 2 models per UD Latin treebank, downloadable from LINDAT and served by the UDPipe REST API.
coverage: latin-ittb/circse/llct/perseus/proiel/udante-ud-2.17-251125
licence_quote: Universal Dependencies 2.17 Models are distributed under the CC BY-NC-SA licence.
accuracy_claim: Lemmas (raw text) UD 2.17: ittb 99.22, llct 97.80, proiel 96.44, circse 89.48, perseus 87.99, udante 87.56.
notes: NC. Useful only as a comparison system. UDPipe 1 models (UD 2.5) likewise 'distributed under the CC BY-NC-SA licence'.

name: LatinCy retrains: la_udpipe_latincy and la_stanza_latincy
what: UDPipe and Stanza model suites retrained by Burns on the LatinCy-harmonised UD treebanks (+ LASLA for the Stanza suite).
coverage: cards: 'UD Latin (6 treebanks)' / 'UD Latin (combined + LASLA)'
licence_quote: license: mit
accuracy_claim: la_stanza_latincy card: Lemmatization accuracy 97.87, UPOS 97.26, UFeats 92.80; la_udpipe_latincy card: Lemmatization F1 92.99, UPOS F1 94.07, UFeats F1 80.82.
notes: MIT tag on weights, same NC-training-data caveat as LatinCy. The Stanza suite's 97.87 lemma accuracy is the highest claim found and is a direct candidate for the 300-token test.

name: Latin BERT (Bamman & Burns 2020)
what: Contextual BERT encoder for Latin (no lemmatiser; case studies for POS tagging and WSD); HF repack at latincy/latin-bert.
coverage: pre-training data table in README: Corpus Thomisticum 14.1M tokens, Internet Archive 561.1M tokens, and others
licence_quote: MIT License  Copyright (c) 2020-2022 David Bamman and Patrick J. Burns
accuracy_claim: HF card (from the paper, Table 1): POS tagging Perseus 95.2%, PROIEL 98.2%, ITTB 99.2%.
notes: HF repack card says 'license: apache-2.0'. Pre-training corpus provenance (Internet Archive scans etc.) is not licence-cleared. Fine-tuning it for lemmatisation would need a gold set — see LASLA/EvaLatin rows.

name: LaBerta / PhilBerta (bowphs)
what: RoBERTa-base Latin (LaBerta, Corpus Corporum) and multilingual Latin/Greek/English (PhilBerta, Open Greek & Latin) encoders; PhilBerta underlies LatinPipe.
coverage: n/a
licence_quote: license: apache-2.0
notes: Encoders only. Also found: KoichiYasuoka/roberta-base-latin-ud-goeswith ('license: "cc-by-sa-4.0"'), POS + dependency only, no lemmas.

name: pie-extended `lasla` model (hipster-philology/nlp-pie-taggers)
what: PIE neural tagger-lemmatiser with a Classical Latin model named `lasla` (download via `pie-extended download lasla`).
coverage: not stated
licence_quote: Mozilla Public License Version 2.0
notes: Code MPL-2.0 (PyPI pie-extended 0.1.5 says MIT). The model's own README path returned 404 and its training data (LASLA) is NC, so the model licence is unverified; ask Thibault Clérice before use.

name: UD_Latin-ITTB
what: Index Thomisticus Treebank (Thomas Aquinas) in UD; lemmas/UPOS/features converted from manual annotation.
coverage: 450,515 annotated tokens (README); genre nonfiction, medieval
licence_quote: The Latin / Index Thomisticus UD treebank is distributed under the same license as the original ITTB, which is CreativeCommons BY-NC-SA 3.0
notes: NC; medieval prose, off-genre for Catullus. Training data of LatinCy, Stanza, UDPipe.

name: UD_Latin-Perseus
what: UD conversion of the Perseus Latin Dependency Treebank 2.1 (lemmas from Morpheus + manual syntax).
coverage: works listed in README: Augustus Res Gestae, Cicero In Catilinam, Jerome Vulgate, Vergil Aeneid, Ovid Metamorphoses, Petronius, Phaedrus, Propertius Elegies, Sallust, Suetonius, Tacitus Historiae — no Catullus, no Horace; token count not given in README
licence_quote: This work is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial- ShareAlike 2.5 Generic License.
notes: NC 2.5 here, although the source repo PerseusDL/treebank_data README says 'Contents of this repository are licensed under a [Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 United States License]' — a conflict to raise with Perseus if the data were to be ingested. Only classical poetry treebank besides CIRCSE (Vergil, Ovid, Propertius).

name: UD_Latin-PROIEL
what: UD conversion of the PROIEL Latin data: Vulgate NT, Caesar BG, Cicero Att. and De officiis I, Palladius, Peregrinatio Aetheriae.
coverage: original PROIEL README token counts: Vulgate 112,454; Caesar 28,607; Cicero Att. 42,855; De officiis 10,644; Palladius 12,148; Peregrinatio 18,356
licence_quote: This work is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial- ShareAlike 4.0 Generic License.
notes: Licence mismatch: LICENSE.txt says 4.0, README metadata says 'License: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0', and the proiel-treebank README says 'freely available under a [Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 License]'. NC either way. Prose only.

name: UD_Latin-LLCT
what: Late Latin Charter Treebank (8th–9th c. Tuscan charters).
licence_quote: The treebank is licensed under the Creative Commons License Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International.
notes: CC BY-SA, but early-medieval legal prose: irrelevant to Catullan vocabulary except as a lemma spelling reference.

name: UD_Latin-UDante
what: Dante's Latin works (De vulgari eloquentia, Monarchia, Letters, Eclogues, Questio) in UD.
coverage: 1,721 sentences, 57,242 syntactic words
licence_quote: The treebank is licensed under the Creative Commons License Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International.
notes: Conflict: LICENSE.txt says CC BY-SA 4.0 but the README says 'The treebank is licensed under the terms of [CC BY-NC-SA 3.0]' and 'License: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0'. Medieval; contains some poetry (Eclogues).

name: UD_Latin-CIRCSE
what: Seneca Hercules Furens, Agamemnon, Oedipus, Phoenissae and Tacitus Germania; lemmas/POS/morphology received from the LASLA Opera Latina corpus, syntax added at CIRCSE.
coverage: five texts; README gives e.g. Hercules Furens 7,714 tokens / 555 sentences; UD v2.14+
licence_quote: The treebank is licensed under the Creative Commons License Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International.
notes: The only CC BY-SA classical verse treebank (Senecan tragedy, Golden/Silver Latin metres). Its LASLA-derived lemma layer is therefore a BY-SA sample of LASLA conventions (u-only orthography) — useful for checking a lemmatiser's lemma spelling and as recorded lemmas for the Seneca choral lyrics in the PRD's minor-poets list.

name: Perseus AGLDT Latin v2.1 (PerseusDL/treebank_data)
what: Original Perseus Latin Dependency Treebank XML (12 files, PHI ids).
coverage: files: phi0448 (Caesar), phi0474 (Cicero), phi0620 (Propertius), phi0631 (Sallust), phi0690 (Vergil), phi0959 (Ovid), phi0972 (Petronius), phi0975 (Phaedrus), phi1221 (Augustus), phi1348 (Suetonius), phi1351 (Tacitus), tlg0031.tlg027 (Vulgate) — no Catullus (phi0472) or Horace (phi0893)
licence_quote: Contents of this repository are licensed under a [Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 United States License](http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/us/).
notes: BY-SA at source vs NC in the UD conversion (see UD_Latin-Perseus). Lemmas are Morpheus-derived.

name: LASLA corpus on GitHub (CIRCSE/LASLA v1.0.1, LiLa linking)
what: The LASLA (Liège) manually verified lemmatised and morphologically tagged classical corpus, published as CoNLL-UP (ID FORM LEMMA UPOS XPOS FEATS … + LILA:FLCAT, LILA:SENTID, LILA:LINE, LiLa lemma id, token URI) and Turtle, with every token linked to the LiLa Lemma Bank.
coverage: Catullus: conllup/Catullus_Catullus_Catul.conllup = 13,129 syntactic words (plus 244 multiword-token lines for enclitic compounds), 3,161 distinct lemma strings, 3.8 MB. Horace complete: Carmina I–IV 4,064 + 2,477 + 4,459 + 2,653, Epodi 3,078, Carmen Saeculare 339, Ars Poetica 3,209, Epistulae 6,883 + 3,264, Sermones 7,132 + 7,449 = 45,007 words. Both poets together 58,136 words, 17.4 MB. Whole repo 248.9 MB, 376 files.
licence_quote: These resources are licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License.
accuracy_claim: Manual: README says 'semi-automatically lemmatized and annotated with morphosyntactical information, with full manual verification'.
notes: The gold standard for the PRD's held-out accuracy check: human-verified lemmas for every Catullus and Horace token, with LiLa ids (e.g. cui → quis lilaLemma:121165). Orthography is u-only and j-less ('nouum', 'iuuat', 'Iupiter'), no punctuation, lemma 'nouus' not 'novus'; enclitic compounds are split into parts under a multiword line. NC + ShareAlike: fine for evaluation, error analysis and training-free comparison; ingesting it as recorded lemmas in the product index needs either acceptance of NC/SA for that data or a request to LASLA/CIRCSE (README: 'LASLA texts are available through data-sharing agreements'). The ULiège page says the texts are freely consultable online ('les textes latins du L.A.S.L.A. sont accessibles gratuitement sur Internet … Opera Latina'); the LASLA Dataverse is robots-blocked and was not fetched. This is also LatinCy's LASLA training source (v1.0.1), so LatinCy must not be scored on it without noting the overlap.

name: EvaLatin 2020/2022/2024 data (CIRCSE/LT4HALA)
what: Shared-task gold data: 2020 lemmatisation/POS (LASLA-derived) incl. Horace Odes as the cross-genre test; 2022 test (Livy, Ovid Met., Pliny NH, Sabellicus); 2024 syntactic parsing test.
coverage: 2020 gold_EvaLatin/Horatius-Carmina_GOLD.conllu: 13,290 tokens, 597 sentences, lemma + UPOS only (feats '_'); other 2020 gold: Caesar BC1, Cicero In Cat., Pliny Ep. 10, Seneca Prov./Vita beata, Tacitus Agr./Germ., Summa c. Gent. IV
licence_quote: The EvaLatin 2020 dataset is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike (CC BY-NC-SA) 4.0 International.
notes: 2022 LICENSE.txt: 'The EvaLatin 2022 dataset is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike (CC BY-NC-SA) 4.0 International.' 2024 LICENSE.txt: 'The EvaLatin 2024 dataset is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike (CC BY-SA) 4.0 International.' (parsing test data only; texts not listed in the README). The Horace Odes gold is the same LASLA annotation as the LASLA repo's HorCarm1–4 (13,653 words), so it adds no new tokens but is a ready-made standard test set used by published systems.

name: Tesserae (tesserae/tesserae and tesserae-v5)
what: Intertext search engine; texts/la holds 744 .tess files (plain text with loci, e.g. '<cat. 1.1>\tCui dono lepidum novum libellum') incl. catullus.carmina.tess (2,402 lines) and all Horace works; lemmatisation happens at index time from data/common/la.lexicon.csv.
coverage: la.lexicon.csv: 1,220,933 rows of FORM,TAG,LEMMA (Morpheus-style 10-position tags, e.g. 'ABACTVS,n--p---mn-,abactus'), 35.9 MB; first 400k rows = 130,347 forms / 34,928 lemmas
notes: Unverified licence: no LICENSE or COPYING file anywhere in tesserae/tesserae (commit 5e0ae30) or tesserae-v5; GitHub reports no licence; the site 'about' page is a JS app with no licence text. Text sources (Perseus vs Latin Library) are not recorded in the .tess files. The lexicon is a form→lemma table without token annotations, so Tesserae does NOT provide lemmatised Catullus/Horace; its value would be the form table, pending a licence answer from the Tesserae team (Buffalo).

name: Perseus-derived and other Latin corpora on Hugging Face
what: Survey of 183 'latin' datasets: NIKAW/ud-latin-r2.15 (all six UD Latin treebanks, per-corpus licences listed), daidalos-project/latin_treebanks_ud_test ('license: cc0-1.0' claimed for UD-derived test data), linhgiang/classical-latin-greek-corpus (Perseus texts, cc-by-sa-4.0), julian-schelb/latin-classical-intertextuality-corpus (apache-2.0; Catullus and Horace texts from 'digital repositories and critical editions'), KaanGoker/dactylic-hexameter-latin-poetry-corpus ('license: mit' but 'sourced from The Latin Library Website').
coverage: no lemmatised Catullus/Horace found; 'lasla' search returns nothing
notes: Licence claims on several of these conflict with their sources (CC0 on NC treebanks; MIT on Latin Library text), so none is a safe source. Not fetched beyond the dataset cards.

name: LatinISE (McGillivray)
what: Lemmatised Latin corpus (Sketch Engine); the GitHub repo holds only processing scripts.
coverage: corpus files not in the repo
notes: Unverified: the repo README is a list of scripts with no licence; the corpus itself was not found as an open download (its texts come from LacusCurtius/IntraText/Musisque Deoque per the literature, which was not checked here).

name: LiLa Lemma Bank (CIRCSE/LiLa_Lemma-Bank; lila-erc.eu)
what: The Linking-Latin knowledge base's canonical lemma list: lemma ids, written representations, inflection class, POS, hypolemmas, variants, LemLat relations; links to LASLA tokens, Latin WordNet, Lewis & Short entries and other lexica through the RDF graph.
coverage: 168,789 lila:Lemma nodes (live SPARQL COUNT on 2026-10-10 against https://lila-erc.eu/sparql/lila_knowledge_base/sparql); dumps in the repo: lila_db.sql.gz 11.0 MB (MariaDB), rdf/lemmaBank.ttl 84.6 MB, lemmaBankMap.ttl
licence_quote: These resources are licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License.
notes: LICENSE file in the repo is the CC BY-SA 4.0 legal text (sha256 7abe19ec…, read from commit 1716c79). GitHub reports CC-BY-SA-4.0. SPARQL endpoint works for machine queries with format=json (the /sparql/ page itself is a JS app); robots.txt disallows /data/, /lodview/, /lodlive/, so lemma pages must not be crawled — use the endpoint or the dumps. Raw README fetch from main/master returned 404 (default branch is master but raw URLs 404ed; read from the clone). The 84.6 MB Turtle dump exceeds this survey's download cap and was not fetched. latincy/latincy-ext (MIT) ships a lila_linker that maps LatinCy lemmas to LiLa ids. This is the natural headword id space for the Latin lemma index.

name: Lewis & Short, A Latin Dictionary (PerseusDL/lexica)
what: TEI XML of Lewis & Short 1879 with senses, citations and headwords carrying vowel quantities.
coverage: lat.ls.perseus-eng2.xml 77.41 MB (Unicode Greek; eng1 = beta code, 77.25 MB); first 400 KB holds 247 entryFree elements; 252 of 319 <orth> in that sample carry macrons/breves (ā, ăb, Ăărōn)

licence_quote: Unless otherwise indicated, all contents of this repository are licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. You must offer Perseus any modifications you make. Perseus provides credit for all accepted changes.

name: Gaffiot 2016 (Gérard Gréco's edition of Félix Gaffiot 1934)
what: Re-typeset French Latin dictionary (PDF/XML editions used by Collatinus and gaffiot.org).
coverage: not established here
notes: Unverified: gaffiot.org serves the dictionary through a JS app with no licence text (its /licence and /a-propos routes return the same app shell); gaffiot.fr is a stub; Gréco's site (gerardgreco.free.fr) refused HTTPS and the article URL tried returned a 404 page whose only licence mark is the site-wide CC BY-SA 3.0 footer, which cannot be read as the dictionary's licence. Internet Archive copies ('Gaffiot2016', 'gaffiot-felix-dictionnaire-latin-francais-2016') are third-party uploads with no licence field and were not used. Collatinus credits 'Gérard Gréco, qui nous a confié son Gaffiot 2016 avant parution'. Ask Gréco / check the PDF's own licence page before any use.

name: Wiktionary Latin via Kaikki (wiktextract)
what: Machine-readable English-Wiktionary Latin entries with senses, inflection tables and form-of links, as JSONL.
coverage: 842,381 distinct word forms; senses by POS: Verb 756,346, Adjective 126,833, Noun 96,588, Adverb 3,674, Numeral 1,438, Pronoun 883 (most verb/adjective 'senses' are inflected-form entries); JSONL 1,231.6 MB (Content-Length)
licence_quote: This data is made available under the same licenses as Wiktionary - both CC-BY-SA and GFDL.
notes: Same source family as the Greek 'Wiktionary quantities' set already ingested (CC BY-SA 4.0 + GFDL on Wiktionary's side). Too large for this box at 97–98 % disk; fetch on the laptop or stream-filter. Gives macronised headwords, principal parts and full paradigms — the best open inflection tables for the form inventory; glosses are short English.

name: Latin WordNet 2.0 (Exeter; ThomasK81/latinwordnet2)
what: Lexico-semantic database: lemmas with morpho codes, URIs, principal parts, prosody, synsets and relations; REST API and weekly CSV exports; being aligned with LiLa.
coverage: API index count 74,795 lemmas; CSV exports: nouns 38,785, verbs 11,007, adjectives 20,093, adverbs 4,909 rows (6.1 MB, plain CSV despite .bz2 names)
licence_quote: All data is made freely available under a [Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0  International (CC BY-SA 4.0)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode) license.
notes: Exeter site: 'The data of the Latin WordNet is made available under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International license.' CSV rows carry prosody (macrons) and principal parts; synset glosses are English WordNet glosses, not Latin-specific. CIRCSE/latinWordnet-revision (manual revisions mapped to PWN 3.1) has no licence text in its README.

name: DCC Latin Core Vocabulary (Dickinson College Commentaries)
what: About 1,000 most frequent Latin headwords with short definitions, part of speech, semantic group and frequency rank; downloadable.
coverage: core list ~1,000 headwords (page: 'Frequency Rank' column; e.g. 'ā ab abs … 21')
licence_quote: The lists are downloadable in various formats and licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License.
notes: Good for the composer's one-line glosses of common words and as a frequency prior.

name: Logeion (University of Chicago)
what: Aggregated dictionary site (L&S, Elementary Lewis, Gaffiot, DGE …).
coverage: n/a
notes: Off limits per docs/plans/logeion-and-form-tables.md (no licence or terms, private API key). Only robots.txt was fetched. Everything open it shows for Latin is available from PerseusDL/lexica directly.

name: Latin macronizer (Alatius/latin-macronizer)

coverage: n/a
